subject: Integration follow-up: SDK auth & 5xx repro steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@finlytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration follow-up: SDK auth & 5xx repro steps

Thanks again for the call this morning, Alex — good to meet your engineering team. Quick recap + next steps so we can unblock the integration testing: 

Summary of discussion:
- Finlytics will integrate Redwood for structured output + embeddings/reranker in the ingestion pipeline. Primary goals: accurate reranking for financial docs, sub-200ms tail latency for short queries, and predictable error handling.
- Current sandbox: SDK v0.9.1, using API key in Authorization header; seeing intermittent 5xx when sending batched reranker requests.

Immediate asks (what we need from you):
1) A minimal reproducible request (curl or SDK snippet) that triggers the 5xx. If possible include the exact payload size and whether streaming was enabled.
2) A support log or request-id from the failed request (we can trace routes/instances).
3) Confirmation of which route/region you hit (us-west vs us-east).

Quick repro tips from our side to try before we dig deeper:
- Use explicit Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
- Try disabling streaming (stream=false) to see whether chunked responses are related
- Increase client timeout to 30s for batched reranker calls while we debug

Sample curl + SDK snippet you can try as a verifier:

curl sample:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_API_KEY>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"reranker-1.0","queries":["Which report has revenue growth?"],"candidates":["doc1","doc2","doc3"],"stream":false}'

Node SDK (v0.9.x) example:
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west' });
await client.rerank({ model: 'reranker-1.0', queries: ['Which report has revenue growth?'], candidates: ['doc1','doc2','doc3'], stream: false, timeout: 30000 });

If you can paste the failing payload and the request-id we’ll triage and prioritize reproduction. I’ll loop Dylan on the engineering side to help with a reproducible testcase.

Next meeting: propose Wed 5/27 10am PT if you want us to join a live repro.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Thanks, Marissa. Attaching the support log and a minimal repro payload that tripped the 5xx on our side. We hit this from us-west (us-west-2) cluster.

Observed behavior:
- 5xx occurs ~10% of batched reranker calls; payloads are 3-8 candidates, typical query length 20-40 tokens.
- We see HTTP 500 with body: {"error":"internal_server_error","message":"runtime failure: nv_decode timeout"}
- Request-id from our proxy: fin-req-20260525-7a2c

Repro payload (redacted):
POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{"model":"reranker-1.0","queries":["Find the most relevant financial summary"],"candidates":["(large base64 doc chunks truncated)","docB","docC"],"stream":false}

We also tried SDK v0.9.0 and v0.9.1 — both show the same 500 at about the same point. We can open a tunnel if you need live repro. Attaching support-log-20260525.txt (contains our proxy logs and the request-id).

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: SDK auth & 5xx repro steps

Hi Alex — thanks for the repro and the log. Quick notes from infra/runtime side after a first pass: 

1) nv_decode timeout sounds like GPU-side decoder stall (could be memory pressure or a large tokenization boundary). Our runtime sometimes sees this with large (base64-embedded) candidate blobs.

Immediate troubleshooting steps to try (cheap checks):
- Try stripping any binary/base64 attachments from the candidate strings and send raw text for a quick repro. If that removes the 500, we'll know the issue is input-size/encoding related.
- Set request header X-Redwood-Debug: true and resend one failing request; that will include instance-level diagnostics in the response (we can use it for root cause).
- Confirm you're not setting Transfer-Encoding: chunked from your proxy. Some proxies mix chunked transfer with our internal streaming path and that causes runtime decode edge cases.
- Reproduce with the following curl (our internal repro command):

curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -H "X-Redwood-Debug: true" 
  -d '{"model":"reranker-1.0","queries":["Find the most relevant financial summary"],"candidates":["docA_text","docB_text"],"stream":false}'

2) Client timeouts — increase to 30s while we reproduce. Some retries from proxy may create overlapping inflight requests and trigger resource contention.

3) SDK note: v0.9.1 has a known bug where streaming fallback toggles incorrectly when candidate payloads contain newline-delimited base64 sections. We pushed a patch in the nightly build; I can share a patched client if you want to test quickly.

I’ll try to reproduce with your exact payload and request-id fin-req-20260525-7a2c. If I can reproduce, I’ll capture the instance trace and escalate to runtime.

-Dylan
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@finlytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: SDK auth & 5xx repro steps

Appreciate the rapid response. I ran the simplified curl you sent and it did not 500 — confirming that base64 candidate blobs are likely the differentiator. I'm attaching the trimmed support log + the proxy trace.

One additional data point: our proxy sets Transfer-Encoding: chunked when a candidate exceeds ~10KB (we stream it downstream). We can try switching to Content-Length, but that will require some changes on our side. If that's the issue, we can either (a) pre-chunk on our end into smaller pieces, (b) use storage references for large docs instead of embedding base64, or (c) request a server-side workaround from Redwood while we change our pipeline.

Request-id for the simplified test: fin-req-20260525-8d4f (no error). Request-id for failing run: fin-req-20260525-7a2c (error).

Attaching trimmed logs. Let me know if you want me to open a temporary tunnel for live repro.

Thanks,
Alex

Great — thanks for confirming the chunked/base64 hypothesis, Alex. Plan from here: 

- Dylan: reproduce with the exact failing payload and request-id fin-req-20260525-7a2c and capture instance trace; if reproducible we’ll prioritize a runtime patch and provide a mitigation.
- Dylan/Vivek: prepare a patched SDK (nightly) to avoid streaming fallback for newline-delimited base64 and share a test build with Finlytics.
- Lauren: follow up with Finlytics on timeline for switching to storage references vs inlined base64 (procurement/engineering alignment).
- Marissa/Vivek: schedule a live repro session Wed 5/27 10am PT if Finlytics wants us to join; otherwise we’ll do asynchronous triage.

Alex — can you please attach the tunnel details if you want a live repro and confirm whether switching to Content-Length is feasible on your proxy this week? Also please share the full failing request body if you’re comfortable (we will handle it under NDA).

I’ll track this in the deal record (DL-10234) and mark as P1 until we have a mitigation. Thanks all for the quick turnaround.

Best,
